mappings.note: Two points on a circle give OA = OB, a quadratic in y, and then the radius. Every step is the distance formula; no section or midpoint idea appears.
Chooses between two bus routes by comparing AC + CB against AB - three distance computations and a comparison. Distance outcome, applied.

Three genuinely different asks: the diagonals meet at their common MIDPOINT (LO-3), the diagonal length is a DISTANCE (LO-1), and the board's AREA is wanted. The area is of a rectangle, which C-4.2-LO-1 does not cover, so it sits at competency level.

The fourth pole D is placed so ABCD is a parallelogram, which is a diagonal-MIDPOINT argument (LO-3); the remaining parts are pole-to-pole DISTANCES (LO-1). Positions are read from a grid the stem does not carry.
Distances between each pair of three stars, and their comparison. Pure distance formula, three times.
Journey lengths SP, SH and HP compared to decide a route. Distance outcome; coordinates are read off a graph.
Most parts are DISTANCES between seats (LO-1), but the last part places D with AD:DB = 4:3, which needs the SECTION formula (LO-2). Both are genuinely exercised.
Compass displacements from the house are turned into coordinates and then into DISTANCES between the landmarks. Distance outcome throughout the parts that are legible in the stem.
Side and diagonal lengths of the assembly formation ABCD, each by the distance formula. Coordinates come from the grid rather than the stem.
Which society is nearest the office, and the society-to-society distances. Comparison of distances from the origin and between points.
Flag positions and the DISTANCE between them (LO-1), then the blue flag exactly halfway, i.e. the MIDPOINT (LO-3). The twin of the earlier sports-day item, with the pots along AB instead of AD.

Parts (i)-(iii) re-read the SAME triangle against three different corners taken as origin - a change-of-origin exercise that no outcome in this frame covers, so CG-4. Parts (iv)-(v) are then distances (LO-1), and the point is that they are unchanged by the shift.
